after.commitMessage:
feat: ninety-nine stages, and a story you are meant to finish empty

Story asks for the whole board now. A stage deals its numbers as groups
that each add to ten, so the deal always comes apart — checked exactly,
by search, at every checkpoint and every seed: 100%. What a player picks
is another matter. A clear that cuts across two groups strands tiles
nothing will ever match:

  1 2 3 4 6 7 8 9   comes apart as (1,9)(2,8)(3,7)(4,6)
  take 1+2+3+4 first and 6 7 8 9 is left with no ten in it

Measured over forty seeds a run: a line that takes any legal move
empties the board 35% of the time on stage 1 and 0% by stage 99; always
taking the longest combination, or always taking pairs, is near zero
throughout; a line that only makes moves keeping the board emptiable
gets there every time, on every stage. Being stuck is a mistake, and
never a fixed strategy's fault.

So a move can be taken back, and that is a resource rather than a
convenience — it is what makes "empty the board" a fair goal. It works
on a dead board too, which is the moment it matters, and the last stage
still carries one: at zero there is no way back from a mistake.

Stars follow: three for an empty board played unaided, two for an empty
board, one as consolation for coming close so a run never hard-locks.

The curve runs 1 to 99 over eleven chapters. Four rows to eleven, loose
groups to rigid pairs, five hints to none, five take-backs to one. The
dial is not size — it is how much a wrong move costs.

Also: five blocks that do not add to ten are refused where they stand.
There is no sixth to come, so the selection was already dead while it
sat there looking alive. The board sways and the five flash red before
they let go — a selection that merely vanished left the player unsure
the tap had registered.
